hold_text: THE WORK IS TIER-1 AND WOULD SELF-LAND; WHAT BLOCKS IT IS THE 403 RELAYS, NOT THE DIFF. Both `add_issue_comment` and `create_pull_request` returned 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' for this session -- the documented write-scope boundary, not the transient MCP drop (`issue_read` on the same repo succeeded). CLAUDE.md's remedy is the two relays, and it says in terms that a 403 is never a reason to skip the board. Using them is what puts files outside TIER1_SURFACE. THE UNVOUCHABLE PATHS, NAMED -- all four (a fourth appeared when the board DONE post was relayed; `automation/board-results/mi-266-engineering-lane-done.txt`): `automation/pr-requests/mi-266-secret-map.json` (the pr-opener request that opened this PR), `automation/pr-results/mi-266-secret-map.txt` (the PR URL the runner wrote back) and `automation/board-results/mi-266-engineering-lane-start.txt` (the board relay's result receipt). The two *-results files were committed by the runner, not by me. `automation/**` is not in TIER1_SURFACE, so the guard cannot certify self-landing and correctly refuses it. Neither file is executable, neither is machinery, and neither can affect the runtime: one is a JSON request already consumed, the other is a URL the runner wrote. I did NOT delete them to buy self-landing -- `board-post.yml`'s header records that the request file is deliberately left in place and that its survival is not evidence of a failed post, so removing them to satisfy a guard would damage a relay contract to win a merge convenience. EVERY OTHER PATH IS INSIDE TIER1_SURFACE: .github/workflows/system-actions.yml, .github/pr-landing/, docs/runbooks/restore-webapp-auth.md, docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md, docs/claude/session-board.json, automation/board-posts/ (the board request itself). WHAT A HUMAN IS ACTUALLY READING FOR, since the hold is procedural rather than risk-driven: confirm that adding a SECRET_* mapping arms nothing. It does not, and that was verified rather than assumed -- the set-env branch (system-actions.yml:1554-1576) was transcribed verbatim and run, and with the Actions secret unset the resolution yields empty and the empty-value guard FAILS the run BEFORE REMOTE_CMD is built, so the VM is never touched. The guard is unchanged and must stay that way; a refusal there is the mechanism functioning, not something to weaken so the keys work ahead of a value. No set-env is dispatched, no VM is mutated, and no secret value appears in this diff, the PR, an issue or a log. ALLOWED_EMAIL is deliberately NOT mapped -- it is not a secret (already in the clear at deploy-candidate.yml:137) and rides env_value normally, so the operator originates TWO values, not three. src/web/api/routers/db_explorer.py's fail-closed behaviour is CORRECT and is untouched. VERIFIED STATE AT THE TIME OF THE MERGE REQUEST, so the human clicking merge is not re-deriving it: scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main reads PASS 57 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 37 locally, and the CI `guards` job concluded SUCCESS on the runner for head 86bb26d (job 103223468598), alongside repo-inventory, pytest-collect, `open`, open-and-automerge and `post`. !! IF THIS PR SHOWS ZERO CHECKS WHEN YOU OPEN IT, READ mergeable_state BEFORE CONCLUDING CI IS BROKEN. This branch uses the board-post and pr-opener relays (forced by a 403 on add_issue_comment and create_pull_request), and each relay commits its result file back as github-actions[bot] -- a GITHUB_TOKEN push, for which GitHub fires no pull_request event. That buries the checks and renders IDENTICALLY to `CI has not started`. It happened on this PR after the board DONE post (head moved to e2d4f3d `board-post: results`), and the fix is one ordinary human-authored commit, which is what this edit is. `unknown`/`blocked` means burial; `dirty` would mean a merge conflict -- different faults, different fixes. !! THE PR BODY IS STALE IN TWO PLACES AND COULD NOT BE CORRECTED -- `update_pull_request` returns the same 403 as `create_pull_request`, so this file is the only surface I can write. Both staleness points are in the flattering-to-correct direction, i.e. the body understates how clean the result is, but a merger reading it will be confused, so: (a) the body's Verification section quotes `PASS 56 / FAIL 1`, which was the true intermediate state when the PR was opened; the final state is PASS 57 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 37, and an even earlier local `FAIL 4` was three `No module named pytest` container gaps, not failures (144 passed once installed). (b) The body says the arming file lands on push #2. IT DOES NOT AND MUST NOT: push #2 established that the relay artifacts put this diff outside TIER1_SURFACE, so the PR went to `hold` and the arming file was deliberately REMOVED -- arming a PR that declares `hold` would be self-contradictory. DO NOT go looking for .github/pr-automerge-requests/mi-266-secret-map-jwt-webapp-password.txt; its absence is correct.
why: Adds SECRET_JWT_SIGNING_KEY + SECRET_WEBAPP_PASSWORD_SHA256 to the SECRET_* map in system-actions.yml, plus docs/runbooks/restore-webapp-auth.md. These two keys were in the exact state TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET was in, and the map's own comment records the precedent: the operator can put a value in Actions and there is no sanctioned path to move it to the VM, because a set-env with a blank env_value resolves EMPTY and the empty-value guard correctly refuses the run. This is that path and nothing more. Target is `env_file: web-api` (ict-web-api.service is the consuming unit and loads /etc/ict-trader/web-api.env; a shared write would also hand both keys to ict-trader-live.service, which has no use for them); both that target and ict-web-api.service are ALREADY allowlisted in scripts/ops/set_env.sh, so no allowlist change is needed or made. The runbook is WRITTEN, NOT EXECUTED: it carries the ordered steps and, more importantly, the measurement contract -- #11780 recorded that an EMPTY login body returns 422 from Pydantic before the handler runs, a probe that would grade the host healthy while it was broken, so every probe here sends a well-formed body and the status ladder is read off routers/auth.py:30-66. That yields a credential-free check: a well-formed request with the correct email and a deliberately WRONG password returns 401 when ALLOWED_EMAIL and WEBAPP_PASSWORD_SHA256 are both live, so a session can prove that half without holding a secret -- while a 401 explicitly does NOT prove JWT_SIGNING_KEY is set, because the handler never reaches issue_token on a bad password. The runbook keeps three facts apart and says to name which you established: auth mints, the gate accepts AND still refuses a no-bearer request, and the tab renders -- the last of which cannot be true until the SPA work ships. Also records a measurement nobody had taken: require_session is attached to FOUR handlers, not two -- /api/bot/db/tables, /api/bot/db/table/{name}, /api/pnl (pnl.py:211) and /api/status (status.py:38) -- and the SPA calls neither of the latter two, so no additional tab is dark and the operator's picture is correct.
